title: fix(metadata-protocol): the dialect arm of `classifyIndexFailure` walks `cause` to the conflict arm's depth (#6848)
body:
Fixes #6848

Implements **disposition 1** from the issue body, per the triage ruling of 2026-08-09 06:50Z: give `indexFailureText` the same bounded `cause`-walking depth `isUniqueViolationError` already has, plus a wrapped-refusal fixture. Disposition 2 (document the asymmetry as deliberate) was explicitly not the ruled path — #6699's ruling scoped *that PR* away from the dialect arm, it did not rule the arm permanent.

## The defect

`classifyIndexFailure` had two arms reading two different wrap-depths. #6699 moved the first arm onto `@objectstack/types`' `isUniqueViolationError`, which follows `error.cause` four levels down because pool and query-builder layers re-throw with the original attached. The second — the dialect arm — kept returning `err.message` and stopping.

So a dialect refusal arriving behind a wrapper (outer prose `Write failed` or `pool query failed`, the actual `near "WHERE": syntax error` one step down `cause`) was graded `failed` instead of `unsupported`.

## Why the consequence is real, not cosmetic

The two consumers of the verdict diverge:

- `view-definition-active-index.ts` disposes of `unsupported` and `failed` identically — keep the previous index, report at `error`. Only the wording differs.
- `overlay-index.ts` has an `unsupported` branch that additionally builds the composite **fallback lookup index** (`buildOverlayFallbackIndexSql`), offered precisely because a dialect that cannot take the partial form should still get the lookup. Under a `failed` verdict that branch never runs, so the fallback is silently not attempted and reports `not-attempted` instead of `ensured` / `refused`.

The wrap depth therefore silently decides whether the degradation target is built at all.

## Dormant, and not a regression

Stated plainly because the issue states it: **nothing in the repo produces the wrapped shape today.** `IndexExec` is `driver.raw(sql)` / `driver.execute(sql)`, and the shipped drivers hand knex's error straight back with the dialect text on the outer message, which is why every pre-existing case matched on the first read. This closes a dormant asymmetry before a wrapping raw-SQL driver can land on it — it is not a live user-facing bug.

It is also **not a regression from #6699**, which only made the contrast visible by deepening the first arm. Before that change the classifier took `message: string`, so the dialect arm read exactly the same single channel.

## What was measured before editing (PM assumptions)

Anchored on function names, not line numbers — this family's anchors have moved twice.

1. **Current address confirmed.** `classifyIndexFailure(error: unknown)` and the private `indexFailureText` are both in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/partial-index-probe.ts`, exactly as the issue describes. Premise still valid.
2. **No reusable helper exists — the walk stays local.** `@objectstack/types` exports `isUniqueViolationError` and `uniqueViolationColumn` only. Its two chain walkers (`matchesUniqueViolation`, `findUniqueViolationColumn`) are **private**, and each answers its own question rather than handing back text; there is no message-collecting helper to reuse. Hoisting one would widen that package's contract for a single consumer — and editing `@objectstack/types` is a declared STOP for this card — so the walk is local, pinned to the same bound, with the reasoning in the doc comment. This is PM assumption 2's fallback branch, taken deliberately.
3. **The bound is 4, and the issue's "four levels" is accurate.** `MAX_CAUSE_DEPTH = 4` in `packages/types/src/unique-violation.ts`, guard `depth > MAX_CAUSE_DEPTH`, top-level call at `depth 0` — so the thrown value plus four wrapper levels below it, five objects read. Mirrored exactly, counted the same way.
4. **Cycle safety — the predicate does NOT guard, and matching it means not guarding either.** `matchesUniqueViolation` keeps **no visited set**; the depth bound is its only cycle protection, and a bound terminates a cycle just as well. The new walk matches that behaviour rather than adding a visited-set the predicate lacks, and there is a test pinning that a self-referential `cause` returns a verdict instead of exhausting the stack. Recorded because PM assumption 4 asked for the real answer, not the expected one.
5. **The dialect regex is untouched** — only the text fed to it.

## One judgement call worth reviewing

The collected levels join with a **newline, never a space**. Two of the dialect alternatives are multi-word (`where clause`, `near "where"`), so a space would let a phrase be synthesised across a wrapper boundary that no single driver ever wrote — an outer message ending in `where` above a cause beginning with `clause` would read as a refusal. A newline cannot match the literal space in those alternatives. There is a test that goes red if the separator is ever changed to a space.

Level-0 behaviour is byte-identical to the old body for every previously reachable shape (string, object with a string `message`, object without one, `null` / `undefined` / number), so no existing verdict moves.

## Reverse verification

Predictions were written down **before** running, in `predictions.md`, then measured.

Method: `git checkout origin/main -- packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/partial-index-probe.ts` (fix out, new tests kept), re-run, restore. No `git stash` at any point.

**Predicted red on revert: the wrapped-refusal fixture, the depth-parity pin, the cyclic-chain refusal case, the end-to-end probe case, and the overlay-index fallback case. Measured: exactly those five test cases went red, no others.**

```
× grades a WRAPPED dialect refusal `unsupported`, not `failed` (#6848)
× reads the dialect arm to exactly the depth the conflict arm reads (#6848)
× terminates on a `cause` chain that loops, exactly as the predicate does (#6848)
× the probe classifies a wrapped refusal, and leaves `detail` the OUTER prose (#6848)
× a POOLED wrapper around the dialect refusal still reaches the fallback index (#6848)
 Tests  5 failed | 39 passed (44)
```

The parity pin's failure output is the clearest statement of the defect — the dialect arm reaching depth 0 only, against the conflict arm's 0..4:

```
AssertionError: expected [ true, false, false, false, …(3) ]
             to deeply equal [ true, true, true, true, true, …(2) ]
```

**Two predictions were recorded up front as green-in-both-directions, and are reported as guards rather than as evidence** — they constrain choices *inside* the new walk, which do not exist before the fix, so they cannot go red on revert:

- the newline-separator test (green before, vacuously — the cause is never read);
- the "arm order holds across the chain" test (green before, because arm 1 already walked). This one is the inversion-risk assertion: it would go red **after** the fix if widening arm 2 had stolen the verdict from arm 1. It stayed green, which is the direction that had to be checked.

**One prediction went unmeasured and is not being claimed.** The parity test's second assertion (the literal profile `[T,T,T,T,T,F,F]`) never executed on the revert run, because the parity equality above it failed first and short-circuited the test. It is measured green with the fix in; its predicted red is unverified.

## Files changed

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/partial-index-probe.ts` — added `MAX_CAUSE_DEPTH` and the private `collectIndexFailureText`; `indexFailureText` now joins the chain. `classifyIndexFailure`'s **body is unchanged** — only its doc comment gained the "Why both arms walk `cause`" note.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/partial-index-probe.test.ts` — five new cases (wrapped refusal, arm order across the chain, depth parity, separator, cycle) plus the end-to-end probe case.
- **Deviation from the declared file surface, declared here:** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/overlay-index.test.ts` — one added test. Test-only, no source change. It pins the *consequence* the issue names (a pooled wrapper reaching `fallback: 'ensured'` rather than `not-attempted`); without it the PR would prove the verdict moved but not that the fallback index is actually reached again.
- `.changeset/index-failure-dialect-cause-walk.md` — patch for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. User-visible: `classifyIndexFailure` is a public export of the package.

Not touched, per the dispatch: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `packages/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, `content/docs/releases/`.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` — **65 files, 820 tests, all passed** (814 pre-existing + 6 new).
- Consumption radius swept: `classifyIndexFailure` / `ensureOverlayStateIndex` / `PartialIndexStatus` have **no code consumers outside `metadata-protocol`** — the three hits in `packages/metadata` are prose in comments.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on all three changed files — clean, exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` — OK, 6467 files. Plus a self-scan of the changed files for the wider control-byte range: no hits.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the package reports 159 errors, **0 of which name any file in this PR** — all are pre-existing debt in unrelated `seed-loader-*` / `sys-metadata-repository.*` tests, which is why this package carries no `typecheck` script and sits in the type-check-debt ledger. Flagged rather than silently omitted.
